# MC Mods Dev Bridge
> **English** | 简体中文 | Status | Architecture | Deployment topology
Turn "the AI finished writing a mod, and now a human has to click through the game" into one executa
ble pipeline: **start a real test server → start a real client → connect + op → run a scenario JSON
→ collect evidence → tear down**, across **Fabric / Forge / NeoForge**.
Target: Minecraft **26.3**, Java **25**, Windows.
> This is **development tooling**, not a mod for players. The probe mod it ships exists only so that
an agent can see and drive a real game.
## What it does
- **Server probe** (`lab/shared/.../ProbeServer.java`): state, commands, blocks / NBT, drops, logs,
tick control, action backend; block reads and writes take a `dim` parameter (unknown dimension → 400

).
- **Client probe** (`lab/shared/.../ClientProbeServer.java` + `action/ClientActionBackend.java`):
UI widget tree, slots, scripted input (click / right-click / keys), screenshots, chat commands, `/c
hat/tail` (the chat and actionbar the client is **currently** showing, so you can assert "it really

appeared on the player's screen").
- **End-to-end orchestration** (`scripts/devrun.ps1`): read the i
nstance registry → start the server → wait for readiness → start the client → connect and op → run t
he scenario step by step → collect evidence → tear down; non-zero exit code on failure. Steps suppor
t `retry` (wait for a state to appear); assertions support exact match (`json`), field contains subs
tring (`contains`), field does **not** contain substring (`notContains`), raw response body contains
substring (`text`), and body does **not** contain substring (`textNot`); both probes expose `GET /m
ods`, which is how a cross-loader setup proves what each side actually loaded. LWJGL natives are ext
racted **once** into `.cache/natives/<mc version>-<arch>/` (guarded by a file lock), so an evidence

directory stays at a few dozen KB of logs instead of ~18 MB.
- **DSH plugin** (`tools/dsh-plugin/mcd
ev-devrun/`): wraps the same orchestration as the `mcdev_devrun` / `mcdev_scenarios` tools, so an ag
ent can call it directly.
## What it does not do
**It provides capabilities, not answers to "what should be tested".**
- **No test cases for any specific mod.** Which features to test, which text to assert, how fine-gra
ined to go — that depends on what you are building at the time. The JSON files in `scenarios/` are *

*examples and self-checks**, not a coverage promise and not a recommended list.
- **It does not repl
ace your own hands-on pass.** Sound effects, the purple transition animation, F3 readouts, UI feel,
how a combo feels — none of that has a data channel, so a human still has to look at the game. The s
uite takes over the part that *can* be verified automatically and leaves the human time for the part

that only a human can judge.
- **It does not decide "good enough" for you.** A green scenario only
means the assertions you wrote hold; it does not mean the feature is complete.
## What this repository does not contain
**No server, client, or loader files.** You prepare those on your own machine, then register them wi
lient, or loader files.** You prepare those on your own machine, then register them with the wizard:
- `instances/` (instance registry, contains local absolute paths) is **not committed**; `scripts/set

up-wizard.ps1` or `scripts/register-instance.ps1` generates it locally.
- `dist/` (build output), `t
mp/`, `lab/*/build/`, `lab/*/.gradle/` are ignored too.

/ Forge / NeoForge; Java 25; "start server + start client + connect + run scenario + collect evidenc

Also:

xt` files inside those skeletons are kept verbatim and are **not** relicensed under this repository'

s Apache-2.0.
- **The DSH plugin layer** is written against DeepSeek Harness's public plugin API; DS

H itself and its packages keep their own licenses.
- Details: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
## Quick start
Requirements: JDK 25; a Minecraft 26.3 server directory you installed yourself (**the level that con

tains `eula.txt` and `server.properties`**).
Client-only setups do not need a server directory — tha
t is what `side: client` in the instance registry is for.
[该节后续省略]
## Reference material (not a capability)
docs/examples/pairedportals/ is **reference material**: it takes one concrete mod (custom portals pa
ired by sign text) and shows *one way to think* when translating features into automatically asserta
ble steps — how to group them, where assertions belong, how to wait for timing, and what has to be c
hecked by eye. Every step carries a `note` saying what it verifies.
It is **not** part of the suite and is **not** run by `devrun` by default: the suite only provides c
apabilities, it does not dictate what you test. Before writing cases for another mod, confirm with t
he user "which features to test, what observable change means success, and what can only be judged b
y eye", then write the steps.
Judgement comes **only from the probes / logs / APIs** (block state, command feedback, mod logs, cli
ent coordinates, …). This tooling does the first-round judgement; it does not replace hands-on testi
ng — sound, animation and feel have no data channel and stay with the human.
